senses.gloss: A sound or remark made by many people at the same time.
examples: The announcement was met with a *chorus* of boos.
A *chorus* of complaints followed the price increase.
There was a *chorus* of approval from the back of the room.

senses.gloss: A close friend (informal, slightly old-fashioned).
examples: He went fishing with an old college *chum*.
The two boys have been *chums* since second grade.
Thanks for the ride, *chum*.

senses.gloss: A Christian service of worship.
examples: *Church* starts at ten on Sunday.
We ran into them right after *church*.
She reads to the kids during *church*.

senses.gloss: A branch of the Christian religion, or the Christian religion as an organized body.
examples: The *church* has spoken out against the new law.
He was raised in the Baptist *church*.
*Churches* across the country are losing members.

senses.gloss: A container in which cream is beaten until it turns into butter.
examples: The farm museum has an old wooden *churn*.
She turned the handle of the *churn* until butter formed.
*Churns* like this one stood in every farm kitchen.

senses.gloss: A person whose thoughts and character stay a mystery to everyone.
examples: After ten years in office he is still a *cipher* to the public.
Her co-workers found her a complete *cipher*.
The novel's narrator remains a *cipher* until the last chapter.

senses.gloss: A group of people connected by friendship or a shared interest.
examples: He is well known in academic *circles*.
She has a small *circle* of close friends.
The story spread quickly through his *circle*.

senses.gloss: A regular round of places or events that someone travels between.
examples: After the book came out she joined the lecture *circuit*.
He plays the club *circuit* in the Midwest.
The tournament is a stop on the pro tennis *circuit*.

senses.gloss: A noisy, chaotic scene in which nothing is done seriously.
examples: The press turned the trial into a *circus*.
Last night's meeting was a complete *circus*.
Reporters made her arrival a media *circus*.

senses.gloss: A statement that something is true, made without proof.
examples: The company's *claims* about the product were never tested.
His *claim* that he was home all evening turned out to be false.
She makes no *claim* to be an expert.

senses.gloss: A right to have or to get something.
examples: The children have a legal *claim* to the property.
He has no *claim* on her money.
Two families laid *claim* to the same piece of land.

senses.gloss: A group of words with its own subject and verb that forms part of a sentence.
examples: This sentence has a main *clause* and a relative *clause*.
Put a comma before the second *clause*.
Learners often join two *clauses* without a conjunction.

senses.gloss: The large pincer of a crab or lobster.
examples: The lobster's *claws* were held shut with rubber bands.
He cracked the crab *claw* with a small mallet.
A crab waved one *claw* at us from the rocks.

senses.gloss: The forked or curved part of a tool or machine that grips and pulls.
examples: Use the *claw* of the hammer to pull that nail out.
The *claw* in the arcade machine dropped the toy every time.
The crane lowered its steel *claw* into the scrap pile.

senses.gloss: Someone whose job is cleaning offices or homes.
examples: The *cleaners* come to the office on Friday nights.
She works as a *cleaner* at the hospital.
Our *cleaner* has a key to the apartment.

senses.gloss: A shop that dry-cleans clothes, usually spoken of in the plural.
examples: My suit is still at the *cleaners*.
Drop the coat off at the *cleaners* on your way in.
The *cleaners* on Third Street closes at six.

senses.gloss: A short sharp sound like two hard things tapping together.
examples: I heard the *click* of the lock behind me.
The pen makes a loud *click* when you press it.
There were two *clicks* on the line before the call dropped.

senses.gloss: A program or computer that connects to a server to get information.
examples: Set up your email *client* to check the new account.
The game *client* is a free download.
Older *clients* can no longer connect to the server.

senses.gloss: The general mood or set of conditions surrounding a situation.
examples: The political *climate* has changed since the election.
Small firms are struggling in the current economic *climate*.
A *climate* of fear kept people from speaking up.

senses.gloss: A plant that grows upward by clinging to a wall or support.
examples: Ivy is a fast *climber* that will cover the fence in a year.
Plant a *climber* at the base of the trellis.
These roses are *climbers* and need something to hold on to.

senses.gloss: A short class in which an expert teaches one particular skill.
examples: The team is running a free pitching *clinic* for kids.
She signed up for a weekend ski *clinic*.
The store holds bike repair *clinics* every spring.

senses.gloss: A short piece taken from a film, show, or recording.
examples: They played a *clip* from the interview on the news.
The *clip* went viral over the weekend.
He posted two *clips* of the concert.

senses.gloss: A container that holds bullets and feeds them into a gun.
examples: The officer loaded a fresh *clip*.
He kept a spare *clip* in his jacket.
The rifle came with two *clips*.

senses.gloss: The shutting down of a business, school, or road, for a time or for good.
examples: The station listed school *closings* all morning.
The *closing* of the plant cost four hundred jobs.
Store *closings* have left the mall half empty.

senses.gloss: A feeling that a painful experience is finally finished.
examples: The verdict gave the family some *closure*.
She wrote him a long letter just to get *closure*.
There is no *closure* for parents whose child is never found.

senses.gloss: A mass of smoke, dust, or tiny particles floating in the air.
examples: The truck left a *cloud* of dust behind it.
A *cloud* of smoke hung over the valley for days.
*Clouds* of insects rose out of the grass.

senses.gloss: Storage and computing power provided over the internet instead of on your own machine.
examples: All my photos are backed up to the *cloud*.
The company moved its records to the *cloud*.
You can open the file from the *cloud* on any device.

senses.gloss: Someone who behaves foolishly or cannot be taken seriously.
examples: Quit acting like a *clown* and sit down.
Some *clown* parked across two spaces.
He was the class *clown* all through high school.

senses.gloss: A place open late at night where people drink and dance to music.
examples: We danced at a *club* downtown until two in the morning.
The band plays small *clubs* around the city.
There's a line outside the *club* every Saturday.

senses.gloss: A long stick with a shaped head, used to hit a golf ball.
examples: He pulled a *club* out of the bag and lined up his shot.
You may carry fourteen *clubs* in a round.
She swung the *club* too hard and missed.

senses.gloss: A thick heavy stick used as a weapon.
examples: The guard carried a wooden *club*.
The protesters were driven back with *clubs*.
He grabbed a branch and used it as a *club*.

senses.gloss: One of the four suits in a deck of cards, marked with a black clover shape.
examples: She led with the ace of *clubs*.
*Clubs* are trump this hand.
I was dealt three *clubs* and two hearts.

senses.gloss: The cheapest class of seats on a plane or train.
examples: We flew *coach* to save money.
Only two seats were left in *coach*.
He upgraded out of *coach* at the gate.

senses.gloss: An ordinary passenger car on a train, or a bus used for long trips.
examples: The last two *coaches* were nearly empty.
A tour *coach* pulled up outside the hotel.
We rode the *coach* from the airport to the resort.

senses.gloss: A large closed carriage pulled by horses.
examples: A *coach* drawn by four horses came up the drive.
The museum keeps a mail *coach* from the 1840s.
*Coaches* stopped at the inn to change horses.

senses.gloss: A layer of paint or another substance spread over a surface.
examples: The door needs a second *coat* of paint.
Give the table a thin *coat* of varnish.
Two *coats* should cover the old color.

senses.gloss: The fur or hair that covers an animal's body.
examples: The dog has a thick winter *coat*.
Brush the horse's *coat* until it shines.
Their *coats* turn white in the fall.

senses.gloss: A baked fruit dessert with a thick crust of dough on top.
examples: She brought a peach *cobbler* to the picnic.
Serve the *cobbler* warm with vanilla ice cream.
There were three blackberry *cobblers* on the table.

senses.gloss: A system of words or symbols used to keep a message secret.
examples: The message was written in *code*.
Analysts finally broke the enemy's *code*.
The two of them talk in a kind of private *code*.

senses.gloss: A set of rules that people, buildings, or work must follow.
examples: The wiring does not meet the local building *code*.
The school has a strict dress *code*.
Every employee signs the company *code* of conduct.

senses.gloss: A group of numbers or letters that identifies something.
examples: Enter the *code* from the text message.
What's the area *code* for Denver?
Each product has its own *code*.

senses.gloss: A friend or supporter who helps someone, often in something questionable.
examples: The mayor and his *cohorts* were indicted last spring.
He showed up with two *cohorts* from the old neighborhood.
Her *cohorts* on the board backed the plan.

senses.gloss: Coins taken as a whole, or the system of coins a country uses.
examples: Silver *coinage* disappeared from circulation.
The country reformed its *coinage* in 1965.
Gold *coinage* was common before paper money.

senses.gloss: Low temperature, especially cold outdoor air.
examples: Come in out of the *cold*.
The *cold* kept us inside all week.
He stood in the bitter *cold* waiting for the bus.

senses.gloss: A band put around an animal's neck to hold a tag or a leash.
examples: The dog slipped out of his *collar* and ran.
Her name and number are on the cat's *collar*.
Both dogs wear *collars* with tracking tags.

senses.gloss: The color of a person's skin, seen as a mark of race.
examples: The law applies to everyone regardless of *color*.
She was the first woman of *color* elected to the seat.
They were judged by the *color* of their skin, not their work.

senses.gloss: The colors that stand for a team, school, or country, usually in the plural.
examples: Fans showed up in the school *colors*.
The team's *colors* are green and gold.
Soldiers raised the regiment's *colors* at dawn.

senses.gloss: A regular piece of writing by the same person in a newspaper or magazine.
examples: She writes a weekly *column* on food.
His *column* runs on Sundays.
The paper dropped two of its *columns* last year.

senses.gloss: One of the vertical sections into which numbers or text are arranged.
examples: Add up the numbers in the third *column*.
The last name goes in the left *column*.
Widen the *columns* so the dates fit.

senses.gloss: A long line of people or vehicles moving one behind another.
examples: A *column* of trucks rolled through the town.
Marchers formed a *column* two miles long.
*Columns* of refugees moved along the highway.

senses.gloss: A performer whose job is making an audience laugh.
examples: The *comic* opened with a joke about the weather.
She's a stand-up *comic* from Chicago.
Three *comics* are on the bill tonight.

senses.gloss: Something said or written to give an opinion.
examples: The senator had no *comment* on the report.
His *comment* about her accent was rude.
She made a few *comments* at the end of the meeting.

senses.gloss: A formal agreement between people, groups, or states.
examples: The states signed a *compact* on water rights.
The settlers drew up a *compact* before going ashore.
Such *compacts* need the approval of Congress.

senses.gloss: A small car, smaller than a full-size model.
examples: We rented a *compact* for the week.
A *compact* is much easier to park downtown.
*Compacts* get far better mileage.

senses.gloss: The central idea or unusual image on which a work of art is built.
examples: The whole film rests on one clever *conceit*.
The novel's *conceit* is that the house tells the story.
The poem builds on an old *conceit* comparing love to war.

senses.gloss: A matter that involves a particular person or is their responsibility.
examples: How I spend my money is not your *concern*.
Safety is the *concern* of every employee here.
Those decisions are the *concern* of the board.

senses.gloss: A business or company.
examples: The bakery is a small family *concern*.
The bank sold the building to a foreign *concern*.
After the merger it was still a going *concern*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing through which something is passed from one place to another.
examples: The charity became a *conduit* for foreign money.
He served as a *conduit* between the two governments.
The port is the main *conduit* for goods from Asia.

senses.gloss: A crisp cone-shaped holder that ice cream is served in.
examples: She ordered two scoops in a *cone*.
My *cone* dripped all down my hand.
The kids picked sugar *cones* instead of cups.

senses.gloss: A bright orange plastic marker set on a road to guide traffic.
examples: *Cones* narrowed the highway to one lane.
A worker set a *cone* behind the truck.
Somebody knocked over the last *cone*.

senses.gloss: The hard scaly seed case of a pine or fir tree.
examples: The kids collected pine *cones* for the wreath.
A squirrel sat on the stump chewing a *cone*.
The tree drops its *cones* in late fall.

senses.gloss: A machine for playing video games on a television.
examples: He got a new *console* for his birthday.
The game runs on every major *console*.
Both *consoles* sold out before Christmas.

senses.gloss: A panel holding the controls and screens for a machine or system.
examples: The engineer sat at the mixing *console*.
A red light came on across the *console*.
Both *consoles* in the control room were manned.

senses.gloss: The state of two things touching each other.
examples: Do not let the wire come into *contact* with water.
The disease spreads through *contact* with the skin.
His hand made *contact* with the hot pan.

senses.gloss: Communication between people who are apart.
examples: We lost *contact* with them after the move.
She has had no *contact* with her father in years.
Stay in *contact* while you're away.

senses.gloss: A thin lens worn on the eye instead of glasses, usually used in the plural.
examples: I wear *contacts* during the week and glasses at night.
One of my *contacts* fell out on the bus.
She keeps a spare *contact* in her bag.

senses.gloss: A person or group in an experiment that gets no treatment, used for comparison.
examples: Half the patients served as the *control*.
The study had no proper *control*.
The *controls* were given a sugar pill instead.

senses.gloss: A small file a website stores in your browser to remember you.
examples: The site asks you to accept *cookies*.
Clear your *cookies* and try logging in again.
A *cookie* keeps you signed in between visits.

senses.gloss: Something made to look exactly like an original.
examples: Make a *copy* of the key for your sister.
The painting on the wall is a very good *copy*.
Send *copies* of the signed form to both offices.

senses.gloss: Written text prepared for printing or for an advertisement.
examples: The ad *copy* needs to be shorter.
She writes *copy* for a marketing firm.
The editor cut half of his *copy*.

senses.gloss: A length of thin rope or thick string.
examples: Tie the box with a piece of *cord*.
The curtains are held back with a silk *cord*.
He cut two *cords* to the same length.

senses.gloss: A measure of cut firewood, a stack four feet high, four feet wide, and eight feet long.
examples: We ordered two *cords* of oak for the winter.
A *cord* of seasoned wood costs more than green wood.
He stacked the *cord* against the barn wall.

senses.gloss: The most important or central part of something.
examples: Trust is at the *core* of any good marriage.
That question goes to the *core* of the problem.
A small *core* of volunteers runs the whole festival.

senses.gloss: The hot center of the earth or of another planet.
examples: The earth's *core* is mostly iron.
Heat moves slowly outward from the *core*.
Scientists study how the *core* makes the magnetic field.

senses.gloss: A small hard painful patch of thickened skin on a toe.
examples: New shoes gave him a *corn* on his little toe.
She soaked her foot to soften the *corn*.
The pharmacy sells pads for *corns*.
